Go subtests (t.Run) are not units: they keep their order inside the parent, are not shuffled by --det-seed, have no own fingerprint, seed or skip decision; table-driven suites (the Go norm) get one fingerprint per whole table.
Benchmarks, examples and fuzz seeds run as Go runs them under --det: no order control, no fingerprint.
Under --det `t.Parallel()` is a no-op: tests run one at a time; a test that needs two parallel subtests to talk to each other hangs unless --det-keep-parallel (which gives up serial determinism).
Under --det Go packages run one at a time (`-p 1`): the default `go test ./...` package parallelism (GOMAXPROCS packages at once) is lost; no parallel-with-proof for Go.
cgo crypto (BoringCrypto / GOEXPERIMENT=boringcrypto, FIPS builds), /dev/urandom opened directly and getrandom from assembly or cgo are not controlled by the crypto control.

The deterministic crypto stream applies to "test builds only" and makes keys/nonces/TLS randomness predictable in tests: tests asserting randomness quality or uniqueness across processes change behaviour.
Map iteration order for maps used by several goroutines at once is deterministic only if the goroutines interleave the same way (not controlled at Level 0).
`select` among channels made ready by other goroutines still depends on the interleaving: the classic Go flake source is only partly controlled.

Go timers and tickers still fire after their real delay (then move the virtual clock): time.After(10*time.Second) costs 10 real seconds, and when a timer fires relative to other goroutines is not controlled.
Deadlines inside the network poller (SetDeadline/SetReadDeadline) keep real time: I/O timeouts are real-time dependent under --det.
`testing/synctest` bubbles keep their own fake clock, outside fenvix's virtual clock and fingerprints.
Go code calling the vDSO or clock_gettime directly (and C code through cgo) reads the real clock under --det.
File access and change times through `Sys()` (Stat_t.Atim/Ctim) are not moved onto the virtual clock (only modification times are).
Statically linked programs a Go test starts (every Go binary built by the test: the norm for CLI projects) keep the real clock; only dynamically linked children get the preloaded clock shim.
Without a C compiler on the machine, child processes of Go tests keep the real clock (the shim is built at run time with cc); only said at start.
A stopped ticker still counts as due, so time.Sleep waits for real: slower than necessary.
Directory listings through raw syscall.Getdents (and x/sys/unix.ReadDirent, used by fastwalk/godirwalk) are not sorted.
UDP `sendto` without connect is not blocked by the closed network.
Raw `syscall.Connect` is not blocked by the closed network.
cgo DNS resolvers (netgo off, CGO_ENABLED=1 default on Linux with glibc) are not guarded: lookups leave the machine.

Network record/replay (cassettes) "is not built for Go yet": a Go test that needs an external service can only be blocked or allowed live, never made reproducible. No --det-record/--det-allow-host flags in fenvix-go usage.
fenvix-go has no `--det-allow-host` option: a Go test that must reach one external host cannot be allowed selectively (only --det-disable=net for everything).
After 32 deterministic ports in use the kernel chooses the port; client-side ephemeral ports are never deterministic.

With the sched control, runtime background goroutines (scavenger, sysmon wakeups, timers) still enter the run queue at real-time-dependent moments, and the netpoller/real timers decide when a blocked goroutine becomes runnable: goroutine order is not fully deterministic ("measured residual in REPORT-2").

The sched control runs test binaries with GOMAXPROCS=1, no async preemption and stop-the-world GC: data races and true-parallel bugs cannot occur (hidden, not reproduced), and CPU-bound parallel tests run on one core.

docs/GO.md describes the `sched` control at line 51 and, two lines later, says "--det does not change GOMAXPROCS ... goroutine interleaving ... not controlled" (pre-sched text left in); the usage text lists controls without `sched`. A reader cannot tell what is controlled.
The pid is controlled only when the run can create a PID namespace (root + util-linux unshare); otherwise "NOT the pid": pid-derived names/seeds stay random on ordinary CI users.
Go skip-with-proof unit is the top-level test; subtests belong to the parent: one changed input reruns the whole table-driven test.

area: Limits / GO.md skip: module root keyed
missing: The module root path is part of the Go skip key: two checkouts (another runner work dir, another machine path) never share results.

area: Limits / GO.md skip: no shared cache
missing: `--skip-cache` takes a local DIR only: there is no URL/shared cache service client for Go (Python and Node have one); promise item "shared cache" is absent for Go.
In Go skip mode a result is reused only on the UTC day it was recorded: every night the whole suite reruns (cache cold at 00:00 UTC). Recorded in DECISIONS 2026-11-19 (virtual-day clock).
decide_for: Recorded 2026-11-19: real clock gave 3-15% reuse; the day key is the sound trade-off
decide_against: A team working across 00:00 UTC (Asia/Pacific daytime) hits a cold cache mid-day; founder may want epoch windows as Python has (--det-cache-epoch-window)

missing: In Go skip mode a fixture that expires later today (certificate NotAfter) still passes under fenvix until the next UTC day: the customer must schedule the nightly `--skip-real-clock` job himself. Recorded in DECISIONS 2026-11-19.
decide_for: Recorded 2026-11-19 with the nightly check as the bound
decide_against: Up to 24 h of a wrong pass, and the nightly job is manual set-up nobody is told to do by the tool

missing: Under fenvix a Go test that depends on a changing field of /proc/1/stat sees constants in every run: its behaviour differs from plain `go test`.

area: Limits / GO.md skip: wall clock without time control
missing: Where the time control is unavailable (Go 1.22, --det-disable=time), any use of a wall time other than comparison with a fixed time (formatting, Unix(), net/http servers and loggers with timestamps) makes the test not reusable.
Go prefix rule: a test depends on everything package init, TestMain and all earlier tests in the binary observed; one changed input early in a package reruns every later test of that package.
A Go test that was skipped (t.Skip) is never reused: it is rerun every time (Python/Node reuse skipped results).
A Go test that connects or sends to a loopback port or unix socket the run did not open itself (service container, local database, docker socket) is never reused: integration suites get 0% skip.
A Go test that starts another program is never reused (its clock and entropy are invisible): CLI projects that exec their own binary get 0% skip.
Without strace installed (or without ptrace permission: default Docker seccomp, hardened CI) nothing is reused in Go skip mode: decisions are only reported.
Go skip capture runs every test binary under strace (ptrace): the cost is said to be "measured in the report" but no number is in docs/GO.md; UNKNOWN overhead on syscall-heavy suites.
A Go test that read any /proc file other than /proc/self and the virtual /proc/1/stat is not reusable.
Go examples (ExampleXxx), benchmarks and fuzz seed corpora are not fingerprinted and never skipped: they always run.
A panicking Go test ends the test binary: the trace records `interrupted` and every later test of the package has no result/fingerprint in that run.

The overlay rebuilds the standard library and every dependency once per toolchain and fenvix version: a cold first run pays a full rebuild ("measured cost in the report", no number in the doc: UNKNOWN).
fenvix-go uses `-exec` itself and refuses a user `-exec` (exit 2): projects that run tests under an emulator or wrapper (qemu, sudo, dlv) cannot use fenvix-go.

Only `go test` is wrapped: gotestsum, ginkgo CLI, `go test -json` consumers work only if they can be pointed at `fenvix-go test`; there is no ginkgo/testify-suite awareness (suite methods are subtests of one top-level test => one unit).

JVM skip with proof is capture + decision only: `fenvix-skip decide A B` says which tests are reusable but Gradle and Maven still run every test; no time is saved. "The decider runs in measurement mode ... an online decider in the runner (not built yet)".
The JVM shell writes no receipts for reused tests and has no --det-cache-verify mode (nothing is reused).
No shared cache for JVM: `fenvix-skip decide` compares two local capture directories; no store, no URL.

fenvix-jvm `run` accepts only --det, --det-seed, --deps, --det-disable, --det-allow-host, --out: no --det-epoch, --det-tick, --det-urandom switch, --det-trace, --det-compare, --det-order, --det-record.
Only gradle/gradlew/mvn/mvnw are accepted ("unknown build tool"): Bazel, sbt, Ant, Mill, `java -jar junit-platform-console`, and wrapper scripts (make test, ./ci.sh) are refused.
The Maven extension rewrites only maven-surefire-plugin: integration tests run by maven-failsafe-plugin (`mvn verify`, *IT classes) get no agent, no --det, no capture.

Brackets exist for the JUnit Platform listener and the JUnit 4 RunNotifier only: TestNG run by Surefire's testng provider or Gradle useTestNG() (not through JUnit Platform) gets no per-test bracket, fingerprint or order control.

Order control exists for Jupiter (class/method orderers) and JUnit 4 ParentRunner only: other JUnit Platform engines (Spock 2, Kotest, jqwik, Cucumber) and ScalaTest get brackets at best, no fixed order or seeded shuffle.
JUnit Jupiter parallel execution is forced off under --det and --deps; one test JVM (Gradle maxParallelForks=1, Maven forkCount=1): no parallel-with-proof for JVM.
docs/JVM.md says the Gradle wiring sets `forkEvery = 0`; the init script keeps the project's forkEvery ("per-class JVM isolation stays") and only sets maxParallelForks = 1.
JDK code that reads the clock itself keeps real time: java.util.logging timestamps, Timer, ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor internals, CompletableFuture.orTimeout/completeOnTimeout.
JNI/native code is not controlled in JVM tests (RocksDB, Netty native transports, SQLite JDBC, Conscrypt).

area: Limits / JVM.md V2 (child processes / other JVMs)
missing: Child processes (ProcessBuilder) and other JVMs started by a test (Testcontainers, forked Spring Boot apps, Gradle TestKit builds) are not controlled.

Threads are not ordered: a JVM test racing threads still differs run to run; the largest class of JVM flakiness (async wait, concurrency: ~half of IDoFT NOD) is only measured (jvm/test/run_l1_measure.py), not controlled.

Kotlin coroutines on Dispatchers.Default/IO are plain threads to fenvix: their interleaving is not controlled; only kotlinx `runTest` virtual time works, untouched by fenvix (its delays are not in the virtual clock).
`new ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor(...)` keeps real time: only executors created through Executors.newScheduledThreadPool/newSingleThreadScheduledExecutor in code under test are virtual.
`java.util.Timer` keeps real time under --det.
Netty event loops and Reactor/RxJava schedulers keep real time (Spring WebFlux, gRPC, Vert.x suites): their scheduled tasks are not on the virtual clock.
No network record/replay for the JVM: the network is closed or allowed per host only; a test that needs an external service cannot be made reproducible.

The JVM closed network guards Socket.connect, SocketChannel.connect and InetAddress lookups: DatagramSocket/DatagramChannel (UDP), AsynchronousSocketChannel, and Netty native epoll/io_uring transports are not listed as guarded.

The "quiet" decision (fast sleeps and timers) samples thread states: a thread woken but not yet scheduled can look idle, so a virtual sleep can return before the other thread ran (a rare false failure / fingerprint difference).

Gradle with JUnit 4 (`useJUnit()`): class order is Gradle's scan order, computed in the Gradle daemon and not controlled; --det-seed shuffles methods only, so class-order victims/polluters are never explored or fixed.

Events of threads born in an earlier test (leaked readers, shared pools created outside tests: every Spring context, connection pool, shared executor) are not part of the current test's fingerprint: non-determinism through shared pools is invisible to the verifier.
JDK classes loaded by the application loader (JDK 8 tools.jar, the attach API) are never rewritten.
Maven + JaCoCo: fenvix defines an empty `argLine` property and keeps @{argLine}; a project that sets argLine through another late-binding property or a profile may lose its own JVM args or the agent.

A loop polling the clock while another thread works gets a clock that follows real time: its clock values are timing-dependent, so fingerprints of busy-wait tests (Awaitility-style polling, the JVM norm for async assertions) are not reproducible.
A JDK timer thread waiting for its next task counts as working: Thread.sleep waits for real while any Timer / scheduled pool task is pending; suites with a background scheduler get no fast sleeps.
A sleep is fast only if no other thread's timed wait would expire before it ends; otherwise real time is waited.
A background thread left running by an earlier test that reads the clock during a later test changes that test's clock values and fingerprint.
SecureRandom subclasses that override nextBytes without calling super (third-party providers: BouncyCastle DRBG, Conscrypt) are not seeded.

Identity hash codes are not controlled: HashMap/HashSet iteration over keys using Object.hashCode (plain objects, enums, Class, lambdas) changes when another seed/order or thread count runs earlier; not in the fingerprint.

NonDex-style "ID" flakiness (code relying on unspecified HashMap/getDeclaredFields/getMethods order) is declared out of Level 0's scope: the JVM shell has no mode that explores iteration orders, although IDoFT's largest JVM category is ID.
decide_for: NonDex needs a patched JDK; scope creep for Level 0
decide_against: Promise 2 (exploration finds hidden bugs): ID is the biggest known JVM flaky class and a seeded iteration order is exactly "hash seeds / map and set order"

missing: Under heavy load the virtual scheduler's real-time fallback lets an extra periodic tick fire: the fingerprint of a fixed-rate timer test differs between two --det runs (1 of 5 loaded pairs, MEASURED by jvm/test/run_d5_load.py). "Not fixable at Level 0".

JVM skip key: objects shared through JUnit extension stores (Spring TestContext cache, Testcontainers singletons, MockK/Mockito state held by extensions) are not keyed: a test reading only these "can be reused wrongly".
JVM skip key: writes to static fields through Unsafe or VarHandle are not seen.
JVM skip key: type annotations (TypeAnnotationParser) are not keyed.

JVM skip key: JDK caches other than resource bundles, bean infos and serialization descriptors are not keyed (MethodType, ClassValue, locale service providers, FileSystems providers, PropertyEditorManager).
JVM skip key: the java.util.logging configuration file read once at LogManager start-up is not keyed.

JVM skip key: thread priority, daemon flag and ThreadLocal values left on the runner thread by JDK code are not keyed (ThreadLocal leaks between tests are a classic order dependency: MDC, SecurityContextHolder, RequestContextHolder).
JVM skip key: ClassLoader assertion status, the security manager and Charset providers are not keyed.
JVM skip key: system properties read by JDK code (not through code under test: file.encoding, user.timezone, java.io.tmpdir, http.proxyHost, line.separator) are not keyed per test.
JVM skip key: a static initialiser racing another thread's first use of a class (the epoch fast path) is not attributed correctly.
JVM skip key: state written asynchronously by a thread an earlier test left running is attributed to whichever test is current.

area: Limits / JVM.md skip: other class loaders
missing: Classpath resource lookups through another class loader "are not keyable (never reused)": tests in OSGi, Spring Boot DevTools restart loaders, custom plugin loaders are never reusable.

area: Limits / JVM.md skip: child process / native
missing: A JVM test that started a child process, loaded a native library from non-JDK code or called a native method of the project is not reusable.
A JVM test that "wrote a file it could read back" or made an external network attempt is not reusable.
Tests of a class with one shared instance (Jupiter PER_CLASS, TestNG, other engines) depend on every earlier test of the class: one change reruns the rest of the class.

A JVM test that read mutable static state is reused only if every earlier test in its JVM is reused or touched no shared static state and the state-touching predecessors are identical and in the same order: in Spring-style suites (static caches everywhere) one rerun cascades to most later tests (reuse share on real projects not stated in docs/JVM.md: UNKNOWN).

area: Limits / JVM.md decide CLI needs Python + blake3
missing: `jvm/skip/fenvix_skip.py` (the documented interface, `python3 jvm/skip/fenvix_skip.py decide`) is a Python script outside the jar; CI installs `pip install blake3` for the JVM tests; a JVM-only team needs Python to get a skip decision.

area: Limits / JVM.md agent native lib Linux x86_64 only
missing: fenvix-agent.jar bundles only `libfenvix_jvm.so` built for the build host (Linux x86_64): the agent cannot load its Rust core on macOS, Windows or Linux arm64 (JVM developers' laptops, Graviton runners).
evidence: jvm/build.sh:13; docs/RELEASE-1.md:49-51 (Linux arm64 "UNKNOWN for Node, Go, JVM") (engine@claude/release-1)

missing: CI tests the agent on JDK 8, 11, 17, 21 only: JDK 25 (LTS, 2025-09) is untested; JDK hooks patch JDK-internal classes (File.normalizedList, UnixFileSystemProvider) that change between releases ("fenvix: JDK hooks not installed" is only printed to stderr and the run goes on without those controls).
Filesystem order for NIO is a hook on `UnixFileSystemProvider.newDirectoryStream`: on Windows (WindowsFileSystemProvider) NIO directory streams are not sorted.
decide_against: JVM shops run CI on Windows more than other ecosystems; the free plugin promise covers any runner

missing: unittest, Django, nose2, ward, zope and doctest shells are serial only under --det: no parallel-with-proof outside pytest-xdist.

`bun test` files are "refused unless the Bun capture covers every API used": any Bun.* API not on the PURE list makes the file uncacheable (flag runtime-api), and an API added by a later Bun is refused until classified by hand.
`deno test` files are refused for caching unless every Deno API used is classified; a function added by a later Deno is not cacheable until classified.

Under --det-cache Mocha, Jasmine and uvu run each test file in a fresh process instead of the suite's single process: a suite whose files depend on shared process state fails under --det-cache while passing under plain runs and under --det ("such a file is reported, never silently reused").

Python runners with no shell: pytest-bdd/behave (behave CLI), tox/nox as runners, trial (Twisted), green, testtools/stestr, avocado, robotframework, lettuce, pytest-xdist `--boxed`/forked, Hypothesis CLI. Only unittest, django, nose2, zope, doctest, ward are listed.
decide_for: The six cover the runners measured in harness/runner_usage; long tail is small
decide_against: behave, trial and stestr have real user bases (OpenStack uses stestr for every project); "any runner" is the promise

missing: Node/front-end runners with no shell: Playwright Test (measure only), Cypress, WebdriverIO, Karma, Jasmine in browser (jasmine-browser-runner), web-test-runner, Storybook test-runner, QUnit, Lab, tape (raw), Cucumber.js, Detox.
unittest (and nose2, zope, doctest, Django) reuse a TestCase class as a whole or not at all: one changed method reruns the whole class.

In-memory state left by a test module's import (a module that patches a library or sets a variable at import time) for tests of other modules is not an input: "a new test module with such side effects is not seen by the tests of the other modules" => they can be reused wrongly. Same limit in the pytest plugin.
`unittest.main()` inside a test module run as a script (`python test_x.py`), the common way small projects run tests, does not go through the driver: no --det, no cache.
Under the virtual clock unittest prints `Ran N tests in 0.000s`: the runner's own duration report is wrong; slow-test detection and --durations are useless under --det.
Django `--parallel N` is forced to 1 under --det: Django suites that rely on parallel workers (Django's own suite, large apps) run serially; no parallel-with-proof for Django's runner.

Every Django test depends on the whole environment (wsgiref.handlers reads every variable at import): any differing environment variable between CI jobs reruns every Django test; "needs the founder's decision on volatile variables". Same under pytest-django.
decide_for: Keying the whole env is the sound default
decide_against: Without a volatile-variable list, cross-job and cross-machine reuse for every Django project is ~0 (GITHUB_RUN_ID, RUNNER_NAME change every job)

missing: Django tests against PostgreSQL/MySQL (the normal production set-up) connect through a socket and are never cached; "the walks use sqlite". Skip-with-proof for real Django projects is unmeasured and near 0.

Django caches that keep file contents in memory across tests beyond templates and translations (static file finders' storages, a project's own caches, lru_cache'd settings) are not inputs of later tests: a later test can be reused after the file changed.
Django sets TZ from settings.TIME_ZONE at start-up; the adversarial TZ test is skipped for Django (tests/test_runners_django.py:138).
nose2's multiprocess plugin (-N/--processes) is refused under --det with exit 4 (UsageError); turned on from a config file its workers are uncontrolled child processes and nothing is reused.
nose2's `layers` plugin is "not wired" (no layer contexts): layer set-up becomes an input of every test (coarse reuse).
zope.testrunner `-j N` is forced to 1 under --det.
A zope layer that cannot be torn down makes zope.testrunner run remaining layers in a subprocess outside the driver: those tests have no detpy fingerprint and are not controlled.
`doctest.testmod()` called from a module's __main__ block is not covered.
Under detpy doctest prints unittest's report instead of doctest's own summary: output differs from the customer's normal run (scripts parsing "N passed and M failed" break).

The ward shell replaces `Suite.generate_test_runs` with a copy of ward 0.68.0b0's loop: any other ward version with a different loop runs detpy's copy of the old loop (wrong behaviour) until "the copy is updated".
Module- and global-scoped ward fixture state mutated by tests is not seen (the pytest rule for wider-scoped fixtures): reuse can be wrong when a fixture object is mutated.

Under --det the Hypothesis example database is switched off: failures saved by earlier runs are not replayed and new failing examples are not saved, so Hypothesis's own "remember the failing example" workflow is lost.
Under --det Hypothesis's local-constants biasing is switched off (providers._get_local_constants returns nothing): examples are weaker at finding bugs that depend on constants in the code under test.
Hypothesis's storage (Unicode table cache) is off under --det: the table is recomputed in every process using text strategies (cost not measured in the doc: UNKNOWN).
Hypothesis `deadline` reads the virtual clock under --det: deadlines no longer measure real slowness (DeadlineExceeded never or spuriously fires depending on clock reads in the test).

The Hypothesis control patches private internals (`hypothesis.core.threadlocal._hypothesis_global_random`, `providers._get_local_constants`): a Hypothesis release that moves them silently drops the control (no version pin, the test importorskips hypothesis and is skipped in the release gate).
Mocha `--parallel`/`--jobs` is off under --det: files run one at a time.
Mocha `--watch` is refused under --det (error).

area: Limits / runners/mocha.md reporters in per-file mode
missing: Under --det-cache Mocha reporters that need the live runner (`progress`, `markdown`, `json-stream`, custom reporters reading runner state) "may misbehave": events are replayed through ParallelBufferedRunner.

area: Limits / runners/mocha.md global fixtures per file
missing: Under --det-cache Mocha `--require` modules, root hooks and global fixtures run once per spec file instead of once per run: a global setup that starts a server/database or seeds data sees N runs (slower, and wrong for set-ups that must run once).

Mocha test order differs between --det (single process, top-level tests of all files first) and --det-cache (per file): another order digest; a failure found under one mode cannot be replayed by order under the other.
Mocha 11 and 12 only; Mocha <= 10 (still the most installed majors) is not stated as supported.

On Node < 22.15 (no module.registerHooks: Node 18, 20 LTS, early 22) detjs node-test has no node:test facade: no shuffle of tests, no forced serial concurrency; only fixed file order. Node 20 LTS users get a degraded shell.
With `--test-global-setup` (Node 24) the whole node:test run is not cached.
`node --test --watch` is refused under --det.
`--test-concurrency` is ignored under --det: files one at a time.
node:test tests that never begin (declared skipped, todo, filtered by a pattern) are in neither the trace nor the receipts: the detjs summary under-counts the suite.
node:test subtests (t.test) belong to their parent test: no own fingerprint or seed.
Jasmine 5-7 only; jasmine <= 4 not supported; `--parallel` removed under --det.

Jasmine --det-seed relies on a source-text hook in jasmine-core (`return order.sort(node.children)`): another jasmine-core build silently keeps declaration order (only a note), so exploration explores nothing.
A Jasmine file containing fdescribe/fit is never recorded as a pass (overall status incomplete): never reused.
jasmine-browser-runner (browser) is not covered ("Level 2").
uvu test files run directly with `node test/x.js` (uvu's documented default usage) are not covered; only `detjs uvu` (the CLI) is.
uvu's runner is hooked by patching its source text when it loads; a uvu build whose source is not recognised makes every file fail-closed (never a pass) and prints "tests are not bracketed".
AVA 6+ only: AVA 5 and older are not supported.
AVA runs with --concurrency=1 --serial under --det: AVA's whole model (concurrent tests within a file, files in parallel) is switched off; concurrency bugs are hidden and wall time is serial.
An AVA test file that uses a shared worker (ava/plugin) is never cached.
The AVA shell patches AVA internals (Runner.prototype.runTest/start/saveSnapshotState, scheduler.failingTestsFirst, RunStatus.emitStateChange): fragile across AVA releases; only AVA 8.4 is tested.
tap 18+ only: tap 16 and older (no @tapjs/run) are refused with an error.
tap subtests cannot be reordered: --det-seed shuffles files only ("documented, not shuffled"); order-dependent subtests within a file are never explored.
tap `before`/`after` scripts make every file of the session uncacheable.
With --det-cache detjs adds --disable-coverage to tap: coverage (which tap enforces by default) is lost in cached runs.
tap runs with --jobs=1 and t.jobs pinned to 1 under --det ("t.jobs=N ignored").

tap with a synchronous module.registerHooks hook breaks t.mockImport on Node 22; detjs switches to asynchronous loader hooks for tap (DETJS_CAPTURE_LOADER=register), a different capture path than the other runners.

`detjs bun-test --det` runs one `bun test` process per file even without the cache (Bun runs all files in one process): tests relying on cross-file globals fail only under detjs, and start-up cost is paid per file.
Refused with --det for Bun: --watch, --hot, --randomize, --seed; --concurrent/--max-concurrency are replaced by --max-concurrency=1 (test.concurrent runs serially).
`--det-record` is refused for Bun: Bun's native connections (fetch, Bun.connect) cannot be recorded or replayed.
`Bun.fetch` cannot be replaced: it is not blocked by the closed network (only noted, file not cached); Bun.sql/Bun.redis/S3 clients are not closed either.

A library that reads BunFile#lastModified without naming Bun.file, or reaches Bun.env through an alias the source scan misses, is not seen: such a file can be reused wrongly (cannot be wrapped in Bun 1.4.4).

area: Limits / runners/bun.md computed require in packages
missing: A failed resolution of a non-literal specifier inside an installed package is not keyed (Bun).

With Bun the trace takes the test body's outcome: a failure only Bun sees (expect.assertions, a failing afterEach) fails the file via exit status but the trace says `passed` for that test: the per-test trace/fingerprint outcome is wrong.
Under Bun any use of node:sqlite makes the file not cached (its bindings cannot be re-pointed).

area: Limits / runners/bun.md Bun.env keys whole env
missing: A module whose source uses Bun.env or import.meta.env keys the whole environment: any env difference reruns it.
Only Bun 1.4.4 is measured; the wrappers depend on which Bun properties are replaceable in that version.

`detjs deno-test` runs one Deno process per file (type check + start-up + one `deno info` per file): std subset 23 s plain parallel vs 75 s under --det (3.3x, MEASURED local NOISY per the doc); first run on a machine 412 s.
Refused with --det for Deno: --watch, --parallel, --shuffle, --seed, --det-record.
Cassette record/replay of Deno's native connections is not built.

area: Limits / runners/deno.md computed import from library
missing: A module loaded at run time by a computed specifier from a remote/npm module that points at a project file is not keyed (Deno): possible wrong reuse.
With Deno a failure only Deno sees (resource/op sanitizers) fails the file through the exit status; the per-test trace outcome can say passed.

Deno has no listing command: detjs re-implements Deno's test discovery rules (globs, deno.json include/exclude, --ignore); verified identical on one project (oak, 21 files) only; a divergence silently runs a different file set.
Under detjs 2 of 3,021 Deno std tests change outcome (tests racing a timer against work: virtual time decides differently): false failures introduced by Level 0.
